title: Mi a Panasza? – Formal Questions at the Doctor

sections.title: The doctor's register
sections.content: A doctor almost always addresses a patient formally, with ön or maga instead of te. That shifts baj to the more clinical panasz ("complaint"), and the possessive suffix on panasz switches to the formal 3rd-person form: Mi a panasza? is literally "what is his/her complaint", but it's the formal way of asking you, the patient, what's wrong.

items.english: Since when have you been feeling unwell (formal)?

sections.content: panasza uses the same -a/-e possessive ending you already met on formal questions like Mi a neve? ("What's your name?", formal) — the same pattern, just applied to a new noun for a new setting.
